speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your sudden abdominal pain, can you please describe the exact location of the pain and rate its severity on a scale from 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and the bloody stools, I am concerned about blood flow to your intestines. Does the pain feel out of proportion to the tenderness when I press on your abdomen, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits other than the bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent myocardial infarction, sudden severe periumbilical pain, and bloody stools, I suspect an acute mesenteric ischemia. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the Abdomen and Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT angiography confirms reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries, which, combined with your recent heart attack and bloody stools, is diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia
